text: My tomato plants have uniformly pale older leaves, starting at the tips, and new growth is much slower than normal.
The oldest leaves on my tomato show yellow tissue between green veins even though the soil is evenly moist.
My tomato is stunted and the lower leaves are developing a dull purple tint; I have not fertilized this bed this season.
Leaf edges on my tomato are yellowing and turning brown while the centers stay green, and the stems seem weak.

New leaves on my tomato are curled and sticky, with clusters of tiny green insects underneath and ants moving between them.
My tomato leaves have fine pale stippling and delicate webbing on their undersides; tiny moving specks are visible up close.
Something is chewing irregular holes through my tomato leaves, and I found dark droppings plus a small caterpillar nearby.
Several tomato leaves contain winding white tunnels, and a tiny larva can be seen inside one of the trails.

Leaves on my tomato are crisping at the edges after several hot days, and the drip emitter beside it appears blocked.
My tomato alternates between drooping and recovering because the raised bed dries out completely between irregular waterings.
